title: Explain the ACID properties (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability) and transaction isolation levels.
shortTitle: ACID Properties and Transaction Isolation Levels
keyPoints: Atomicity means all statements in a transaction succeed together or none do, implemented with an undo log.
Consistency means a transaction moves the database from one valid state to another, never violating constraints.
Isolation means concurrent transactions behave as if they ran serially, tuned by isolation levels.
Durability means committed data survives crashes, achieved by flushing the write-ahead log before acknowledging.
The four isolation levels are Read Uncommitted, Read Committed (common default), Repeatable Read (MySQL default), and Serializable (strictest).
Higher isolation prevents more anomalies (dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, phantoms) but reduces concurrency.
Modern databases use MVCC so readers do not block writers, and Serializable transactions can abort with serialization failures.

s1_definition.oneliner: Atomicity is all-or-nothing, Consistency keeps rules valid, Isolation keeps concurrent transactions from interfering, Durability survives crashes – and isolation levels tune the Isolation strictness.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Atomicity** – all statements in a transaction succeed together or none do; implemented with an undo log that can revert partial changes.
- **Consistency** – every committed transaction leaves the database satisfying all defined rules (constraints, foreign keys, checks).
- **Isolation** – concurrent transactions produce a result as if they ran in some serial order; tuned by isolation levels.
- **Durability** – once `COMMIT` returns, the changes are permanently recorded and survive crashes, achieved by flushing the WAL before acknowledging.
- **Isolation levels** – Read Uncommitted, Read Committed, Repeatable Read, Serializable – each prevents progressively more concurrency anomalies at the cost of reduced concurrency.
s1_definition.analogy: When Rajesh transfers money to Priya at National Bank of India, the debit from Rajesh and the credit to Priya must both happen or neither – never only the debit (Atomicity). The books must always balance and no rule is broken (Consistency). If two transfers run at once, neither should see the other's half-finished work (Isolation). And once the receipt prints "done," a power cut must not undo it (Durability). Isolation levels are how strictly the bank forbids one teller from peeking at another's unfinished paperwork.

sections.s6_takeaway:
ACID is the set of guarantees a reliable transaction provides. Atomicity means all-or-nothing: every statement commits together or the whole transaction rolls back, implemented with an undo log, so a transfer never leaves money debited but not credited. Consistency means each committed transaction leaves the database satisfying all its constraints. Isolation means concurrent transactions behave as if they ran serially. Durability means once commit returns, the changes survive a crash, achieved by flushing a write-ahead log before acknowledging.

Isolation levels tune how much concurrency anomaly is allowed. Read Uncommitted permits dirty reads. Read Committed stops dirty reads and is the common default in PostgreSQL and Oracle. Repeatable Read also stops non-repeatable reads and is the default in MySQL InnoDB. Serializable prevents all anomalies by making transactions behave as if run one at a time, at the cost of more locking or serialization failures that force retries.

At National Bank of India, two historical failures drove the team's understanding of ACID: a crash after the debit but before the credit (atomicity failure fixed by wrapping both in one transaction), and two concurrent transfers that both read the old balance and overdrew the account (lost update fixed by locking the affected rows with `SELECT FOR UPDATE`). The senior approach is to pick the lowest isolation level that protects the invariant and prefer targeted row locking over globally serialising everything. Modern databases use MVCC so readers do not block writers, and Serializable transactions can abort with serialization failures that the application must retry.

Remember one sentence: Atomicity is all-or-nothing, Consistency keeps rules valid, Isolation stops concurrent interference, Durability survives crashes, and isolation levels trade strictness against concurrency.
